mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate trend over the past 3 months indicates an accommodative monetary policy shift, which reduces equity discount rates and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% over a 3-month period, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce corporate profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where UNRATE > 4.5.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market (PAYEMS growth > 0.5%) combined with weak housing starts (HOUST < 1600) indicates an overheating economy with misallocated resources, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and HOUST < 1600.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) above 370,000 million dollars signals strong consumer spending that supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods classified as late-cycle expansion with RSAFS > 370,000.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production trend (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output and economic activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where INDPRO has been rising for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0% for three consecutive months, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS > 5.0 for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE declines and PAYEMS increases.

mechanism_narrative: In high consumer spending regimes (RSAFS > 370,000 million dollars), a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals reduced demand for durable goods, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where RSAFS > 370,000 and HOUST declines.
